title: openclaw-ops fleet config
description: Frozen snapshot of autodetection plus the decisions autodetection cannot make. Lives OUTSIDE the plugin repository, mode 0600. Resolution ladder: $OPENCLAW_OPS_CONFIG -> ./.openclaw-ops.json -> ~/.config/openclaw-ops/fleet.json -> /etc/openclaw-ops/fleet.json.

version.description: Config format version. 1 is the only accepted value.

host_fingerprint.description: sha256(/etc/machine-id)[0:16] of the host this config was written on. A mismatch puts the plugin in read-only mode: the config describes a different machine, so every path in it is a guess. Omit only when the host has no machine-id.

host_label.description: Free-text label for the host, shown in reports. Not used for matching.

generated_at.description: ISO-8601 timestamp of the last /init write.

project_prefix.description: Compose project-name prefix that selects this fleet, e.g. "openclaw-". Instance name = project name with the prefix removed.

compose_root.description: Directory holding the per-instance compose project directories. Detected from ConfigFiles; recorded so a stopped instance is still locatable.

data_root.description: Directory holding per-instance state trees. Recorded for the same reason as compose_root; never used in place of the live mount table.

gateway_service.description: Compose service name of the gateway container. Detected per instance; this is only the fallback for a stopped project.

reference.description: Instance name used as the clone source and the config baseline. Selector @reference resolves to it.

policy.description: Operator decisions that autodetection cannot make.

update_channel.description: Release channel the fleet follows, by operator name. Resolved through npm dist-tags, never through semver-max or GitHub release ordering — and the two vocabularies are not spelled alike: channel 'stable' resolves through dist-tag 'latest'. Put the channel name here, never the dist-tag.

soak_days.description: Minimum days between a version being promoted on the channel and this fleet accepting it. A correction release on the same line resets the clock.

canary.description: Instance that takes any multi-instance mutation first. Must be the least critical instance and must not be the reference.

stale_log_hours.description: Log silence after which a running, health-green instance is called a zombie.

batch_max.description: Hard cap on instances touched by one batch mutation, canary included.

snapshot_dir.description: Where the plugin writes its own pre-mutation snapshots, outside the CLI's own .bak ring so an automated edit can never evict the human's last-known-good file.

lock_dir.description: Where the plugin keeps its fleet-wide front locks. Defaults to the locks sibling of snapshot_dir, else the XDG state home. Host-local state: the lock serialises fleet-level credential work across instances, which the runtime's own per-state-dir lock cannot do.

snapshot_keep.description: How many plugin snapshots to keep per file.

loopback_only.description: Assert every published gateway port must bind to loopback. A non-loopback publish becomes a security finding.

provisioner.description: Optional external command that mints credentials for a newly cloned instance (machine identity, secret-store access, provider logins). This plugin never handles secret values, so cloning stops at the file layout and delegates the rest here; when absent, the remaining steps are printed for a human. Placeholders {name} {reference} {project} {port} {state_dir} {compose_file} are substituted into args.

command.description: Executable to run. No shell is used, so no quoting or redirection is interpreted.

notes.description: What this provisioner does and does not cover, shown in the clone plan.

instances.description: Per-instance decisions, keyed by instance name (project name minus project_prefix). An instance discovered on the host but absent here is reported as unmanaged, never hidden.

manage.description: false makes the instance read-only for this plugin: it stays in the inventory and every mutation targeting it is refused.

role.description: reference = clone source and config baseline; canary = first target of any batch; standard = ordinary member; legacy = different layout, refuse to mutate; neighbour = not part of this fleet.

criticality.description: Blast-radius hint used to order waves and to require a separate window for the highest tier.

aliases.description: Extra names the selector accepts for this instance.

secrets.description: How secrets reach this instance. Names and locations only — never values.

provider.description: Secret-delivery mechanism wrapping the gateway command.

identity_file.description: Path to the machine-identity file used by the delivery wrapper.

project_id.description: Secret-store project id this instance reads from. An instance receiving far fewer keys than its siblings usually has the wrong one.

expected_key_count.description: Key count a healthy delivery produces. Compared by count and by name, never by value.

notes.description: Free-text operator note carried into reports.
